text: By daylight the pattern is quiet and dull, but at night, in any kind of light, it becomes bars, and the woman behind it is as plain as can be. <break time="0.8s" /> I can see her shaking the bars hard, as if she wanted to climb through, but nobody could climb through such a pattern, for it holds so tightly. <break time="0.8s" /> There are things in that paper that nobody knows but me, or ever will, and I do not intend to tell John, since it does not do to trust people too much. <break time="0.8s" /> Both John and Jennie are secretly affected by the paper, I believe, for I once caught Jennie with her hand on it, and she said it stained everything it touched. <break time="0.8s" /> There is something else about that paper, the smell, which creeps all over the house, waiting for me on the stairs and getting into my hair. <break time="0.8s" /> The only thing that I can think of that it is like is the color of the paper itself, a yellow smell, the most enduring odor I have ever met. <break time="0.8s" /> There is also a very funny mark low down on the wall, near the mopboard, a long, straight, even smooch, as if it had been rubbed over and over. <break time="0.8s" /> I think the woman gets out in the daytime, because I have seen her from every window, creeping along the road and hiding under the blackberry vines. <break time="0.8s" /> I do not blame her a bit, since it must be very humiliating to be caught creeping by daylight, and I always lock the door when I do it myself.
